cohort: Women who underwent elective induction of labor at a large volume obstetrics hospital (July 1, 2011, to June 30, 2013)
finding: The implementation of a 'hard stop' policy aimed at eliminating elective inductions before 39 weeks did not affect the rate of cesarean birth.
mod_finding: Implementing a "hard stop" policy to eliminate elective inductions before 39 weeks did not affect the rate of cesarean birth.
